scene.note: The tokenizer now reads prices and names the way JSON writes them, and refuses anything that only looks like one.

steps.note: The ink supplier's list comes in, with the price of press wash written with an exponent.
tokenize meets a digit and hands the rest to readNumber, which walks the rules: a minus, the whole part, a fraction, an exponent.
Where a part needs a digit and has none, it stops with a JsonError. Otherwise it knows exactly where the number ends.
The characters it read become one number token, and tokenize carries on from its end.
The paper supplier's list comes in, with a name that holds quotes of its own.
tokenize meets a quote and hands the rest to readString, which collects characters until the closing quote.
A backslash is never kept: it says what the next character means, so the quotes inside the name stay in the name.
The whole name becomes one text token, ending just after its closing quote.
A name arrives with an accented letter written as a backslash, a u and four hex digits.
readString checks the four characters are hex digits and turns their code into the letter.
A text that reaches the end of the input without a closing quote, or holds a raw line break, stops with a JsonError.
Every name that does close becomes a text token with the letters it stands for.
